supersedes.reason: The originally named validation split was exposed before Candidate-v4 freeze and is therefore disqualified as protected validation. All architecture, metrics, thresholds, tuning limits, negative-result rules, and zero-cost/sealed-final constraints remain unchanged.

research_question: Can a post-retrieval answerability mechanism distinguish relevant-looking evidence from evidence sufficient to answer, while preserving frozen Candidate-v2 retrieval quality?

architecture.retriever: pse_candidate_v2_rank frozen comparator; no ranking-semantic modification
architecture.answerability_layer: deterministic proposition and slot coverage with contradiction/uncertainty resolution
architecture.integration_rule: SUPPORTED returns the original frozen Candidate-v2 ranking unchanged; CONTRADICTED or INSUFFICIENT returns an empty ranking.

new_validation_requirements: category-balanced enough to exercise direct support, updates, temporal constraints, wrong-field near matches, query echo, unresolved contradiction, partial evidence and paraphrase
dataset and manifest frozen before the one-time run
no Candidate-v4 source changes after observing any result
one execution only unless an operationally transient failure occurs before scientific output

confirmatory_boundary.candidate_v4_confirmatory_benchmark: must be newly created only after one-time protected validation PASS

statistics_rule: Future v6 primary comparisons use 10,000 paired bootstrap iterations for v4-v2 and v4-exact-A-MEM; abstention/error rates report Wilson 95% CIs.
negative_result_rule: If the new one-time frozen validation fails, Candidate-v4 is REJECTED and must not be patched; any new method becomes Candidate-v5.
claim_boundary: This pre-freeze supersession changes only the invalid protected-validation source boundary. It does not change Candidate-v4 source, architecture, selection metrics, thresholds, or acceptance guardrails after seeing a protected result.
